texts.facts: The respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed. 10. In order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of canter, the petitioner produced Ex.P1 & 2 - FIR and First Information is lodged by the petitioner himself police on 14.02.2023. On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC. The FIR is registered against the driver of canter alleging that the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving. The respondent No.1 contended that the accident took place due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle. The jurisdictional police appears to have conducted the investigation and filed the final report against the driver of canter, as per Ex.P.6, for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of IMV Act. The respondent No.1 denied the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of canter and contended that the accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle. The allegations made in FIR and final report does not appear to have been challenged, either by driver or owner of the canter, in any manner. In the FIR as well as final report, the cause of accident is stated to be rash and negligent driving of canter by its driver. Respondent No.1 not placed any materials to rebut or contradict the documents furnished on behalf of petitioner. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials to prove that there is no negligence on the part of driver of canter. If there is negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle, then final report could not have been filed against the driver of canter. No materials are placed to rebut or controvert the said documents or the recitals mentioned therein. The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
texts.arguments: The bills produced by petitioner totally amounts to Rs.4,29,559/-. The respondents not furnished any cogent and satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to medical expenses incurred by him. The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent and satisfactory materials.
